english: I Laud Agni, the chosen Priest, God, minister of sacrifice,
Worthy is Agni to be praised by living as by ancient seers.
Through Agni man obtaineth wealth, yea, plenty waxing day by day,
Agni, the perfect sacrifice which thou encompassest about
May Agni, sapient-minded Priest, truthful, most gloriously great,
Whatever blessing, Agni, thou wilt grant unto thy worshipper,
To thee, dispeller of the night, O Agni, day by day with prayer
Ruler of sacrifices, guard of Law eternal, radiant One,
Be to us easy of approach, even as a father to his son:
YE Aśvins, rich in treasure, Lords of splendour, having nimble hands,
Ye Aśvins, rich in wondrous deeds, ye heroes worthy of our praise,
Nāsatyas, wonder-workers, yours are these libations with clipt grass:
O Indra marvellously bright, come, these libations long for thee,
Urged by the holy singer, sped by song, come, Indra, to the prayers,
Approach, O Indra, hasting thee, Lord of Bay Horses, to the prayers.
Ye Viśvedevas, who protect, reward, and cherish men, approach
Ye Viśvedevas, swift at work, come hither quickly to the draught,
The Viśvedevas, changing shape like serpents, fearless, void of guile,
Wealthy in spoil, enriched with hymns, may bright [Sarasvatī](https://www.sacred-texts.com/hin/rigveda/errata.htm#0) desire,
Inciter of all pleasant songs, inspirer of all gracious thought,
Sarasvatī, the mighty flood,—she with her light illuminates,

We call the Aśvins Twain, the Gods borne in a noble car, the best
Dropping with honey is your whip, Aśvins, and full of pleasantness
As ye go thither in your car, not far, O Aśvins, is the home
For my protection I invoke the golden-handed Savitar.
That he may send us succour, praise the Waters’ Offspring Savitar:
We call on him, distributer of wondrous bounty and of wealth,
Come hither, friends, and seat yourselves Savitar, to be praised by us,
O Agni, hither bring to us the willing Spouses of the Gods,
Most youthful Agni, hither bring their Spouses, Hotrā, Bhāratī,
Spouses of Heroes, Goddesses, with whole wings may they come to us
Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, and Agnāyī hither I invite,
May Heaven and Earth, the Mighty Pair, bedew for us our sacrifice,
Their water rich with fatness, there in the Gandharva's steadfast place,
Thornless be thou, O Earth, spread wide before us for a dwelling-place:
The Gods be gracious unto us even from the place whence Viṣṇu strode
Through all this world strode Viṣṇu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole
Viṣṇu, the Guardian, he whom none deceiveth, made three steps; thenceforth
Look ye on Viṣṇu's works, whereby the Friend of Indra, close-allied,
The princes evermore behold that loftiest place where Viṣṇu is,
This, Viṣṇu's station most sublime, the singers, ever vigilant,
MAY powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered, and victorious,
May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods.
We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Dakṣa, Mitra, Aditi,
May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven,
Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul,
Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pūṣan prosper us, the Master of all wealth.
The Maruts, Sons of Pṛśni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites,
Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones.
A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay;
Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son.
MAY Varuṇa with guidance straight, and Mitra lead us, he who knows,
For they are dealers forth of wealth, and, not deluded, with their might
Shelter may they vouchsafe to us, Immortal Gods to mortal men,
May they mark out our paths to bliss, Indra, the Maruts, Pūṣan,
Yea, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, ye who run your course, enrich our hymns with kine;
The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the Law
Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere;
May the tall tree be full of sweets for us, and full of sweets the Sun:
Be Mitra gracious unto us, and Varuṇa and Aryaman:
THE brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni.
Like as a young man followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess:
Auspicious are the Sun's Bay-coloured Horses, bright, changing hues, meet for our shouts of triumph.
This is the Godhead, this might of Sūrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished.
In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuṇa and Mitra may behold it.
This day, O Gods, while Sūrya is ascending, deliver us from trouble and dishonour.
I WILL declare the mighty deeds of Viṣṇu, of him who measured out the earthly regions,
For this his mighty deed is Viṣṇu lauded, like some wild beast, dread, prowling, mountain-roaming;
Let the hymn lift itself as strength to Viṣṇu, the Bull far-striding, dwelling on the mountains,
Him whose three places that are filled with sweetness, imperishable, joy as it may list them,
May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy.
Fain would we go unto your dwelling-places where there are many-horned and nimble oxen,
To the great Hero, him who sets his mind thereon, and Viṣṇu, praise aloud in song your draught of juice,—
Your Soma-drinker keeps afar your furious rush, Indra and Viṣṇu, when ye come with all your might.
These offerings increase his mighty manly strength: he brings both Parents down to share the genial flow.
We laud this manly power of him the Mighty One, preserver, inoffensive, bounteous and benign;
A mortal man, when he beholds two steps of him who looks upon the light, is restless with amaze.
He, like a rounded wheel, hath in swift motion set his ninety racing steeds together with the four.
FAR-SHINING, widely famed, going thy wonted way, fed with the oil, be helpful. Mitra-like, to us.
He who brings gifts to him the Ancient and the Last, to Viṣṇu who ordains, together with his Spouse,
Him have ye satisfied, singers, as well as ye know, primeval germ of Order even from his birth.
The Sovran Varuṇa and both the Aśvins wait on this the will of him who guides the Marut host.
Even he the Heavenly One who came for fellowship, Viṣṇu to Indra, godly to the godlier,
OF this benignant Priest, with eld grey-coloured, the brother midmost of the three is lightning.
Seven to the one-wheeled chariot yoke the Courser; bearing seven names the single Courser draws it.
The seven who on the seven-wheeled car are mounted have horses, seven in tale, who draw them onward.
Who hath beheld him as he sprang to being, seen how the boneless One supports the bony?
Unripe in mind, in spirit undiscerning, I ask of these the Gods’ established places;
I ask, unknowing, those who know, the sages, as one all ignorant for sake of knowledge,
Let him who knoweth presently declare it, this lovely Bird's securely founded station.
The Mother gave the Sire his share of Order: with thought, at first, she wedded him in spirit.
Yoked was the Mother to the boon Cow's car-pole: in the dank rows of cloud the Infant rested.
Bearing three Mothers and three Fathers, single he stood erect: they never make him weary.
Formed with twelve spokes, by length of time, unweakened, rolls round the heaven this wheel of during Order.
They call him in the farther half of heaven the Sire five-footed, of twelve forms, wealthy in watery store.
Upon this five-spoked wheel revolving ever all living creatures rest and are dependent.
The wheel revolves, unwasting, with its felly: ten draw it, yoked to the far-stretching car-pole.
Of the co-born they call the seventh single-born; the six twin pairs are called Ṛṣis, Children of Gods.
They told me these were males, though truly females: he who hath eyes sees this, the blind discerns not.
Beneath the upper realm, above this lower, bearing her calf at foot the Cow hath risen.
Who, that the father of this Calf discerneth beneath the upper realm, above the lower,
Those that come hitherward they call departing, those that depart they call directed hither.
Two Birds with fair wings, knit with bonds of friendship, in the same sheltering tree have found a refuge.
Where those fine Birds hymn ceaselessly their portion of life eternal, and the sacred synods,
The, tree whereon the fine Birds eat the sweetness, where they all rest and procreate their offspring,—
How on the Gāyatrī the Gāyatrī was based, how from the Triṣṭup they fashioned the Triṣṭup forth,
With Gāyatrī he measures out the praise-song, Sāma with praise-song, triplet with the Triṣṭup.
With Jagatī the flood in heaven he stablished, and saw the Sun in the Rathantara Sāman.
I invocate the milch-cow good for milking so that the milker, deft of hand, may drain her.
She, lady of all treasure, is come hither yearning in spirit for her calf and lowing.
The cow hath lowed after her blinking youngling; she licks his forehead, as she lows, to form it.
He also snorts, by whom encompassed round the Cow laws as she clings unto the shedder of the rain.
That which hath breath and speed and life and motion lies firmly stablished in the midst of houses.
I saw the Herdsman, him who never stumbles, approaching by his pathways and departing.
He who hath made him cloth not comprehend him: from him who saw him surely is he hidden.
Dyaus is my Father, my begetter: kinship is here. This great earth is my kin and Mother.
I ask thee of the earth's extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee.
This altar is the earth's extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world's centre.
Seven germs unripened yet are heaven's prolific seed: their functions they maintain by Viṣṇu's ordinance.
What thing I truly am I know not clearly: mysterious, fettered in my mind I wander.
Back, forward goes he, grasped by strength inherent, the Immortal born the brother of the mortal
Upon what syllable of holy praise-song, as twere their highest heaven, the Gods repose them,—
[Fortunate](https://www.sacred-texts.com/hin/rigveda/errata.htm#5) mayst thou be with goodly pasture, and may we also be exceeding wealthy.
Forming the water-floods, the buffalo hath lowed, one-footed or two-footed or four-footed, she,
From her descend in streams the seas of water; thereby the world's four regions have their being,
I saw from far away the smoke of fuel with spires that rose on high o’er that beneath it.
Three with long tresses show in ordered season. One of them sheareth when the year is ended.
Speech hath been measured out in four divisions, the Brahmans who have understanding know them.
They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutmān.
Dark the descent: the birds are golden-coloured; up to the heaven they fly robed in the waters.
Twelve are the fellies, and the wheel is single; three are the naves. What man hath understood it?
That breast of thine exhaustless, spring of pleasure, wherewith thou feedest all things that are choicest,
By means of sacrifice the Gods accomplished their sacrifice: these were the earliest ordinances.
Uniform, with the passing days, this water mounts and fails again.
The Bird Celestial, vast with noble pinion, the lovely germ of plants, the germ of waters,
THOU, Agni, shining in thy glory through the days, art brought to life from out the waters, from the stone:
Thine is the Herald's task and Cleanser's duly timed; Leader art thou, and Kindler for the pious man.
Hero of Heroes, Agni! Thou art Indra, thou art Viṣṇu of the Mighty Stride, adorable:
Agni, thou art King Varuṇa whose laws stand fast; as Mitra, Wonder-Worker, thou must be implored.
Thou givest strength, as Tvaṣṭar, to the worshipper: thou wielding Mitra's power hast kinship with the Dames.
Rudra art thou, the Asura of mighty heaven: thou art the Maruts’ host, thou art the Lord of food,
Giver of wealth art thou to him who honours thee; thou art God Savitar, granter of precious things.
To thee, the people's Lord within the house, the folk press forward to their King most graciously inclined.
Agni, men seek thee as a Father with their prayers, win thee, bright-formed, to brotherhood with holy act.
A Ṛbhu art thou, Agni, near to be adored thou art the Sovran Lord of foodful spoil and wealth.
Thou, God, art Aditi to him who offers gifts: thou, Hotrā, Bhāratī, art strengthened by the song.
Thou, Agni, cherished well, art highest vital power; in thy delightful hue are glories visible.
Thee, Agni, have the Ādityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue.
By thee, O Agni, all the Immortal guileless Gods cat with thy mouth the oblation that is offered them.
With these thou art united, Agni; yea thou, God of noble birth, surpassest them in majesty,
The princely worshippers who send to those who sing thy praise, O Agni, guerdon graced with kine and steeds,—
HE who, just born, chief God of lofty spirit by power and might became the Gods’ protector,
He who fixed fast and firm the earth that staggered, and set at rest the agitated mountains,
Who slew the Dragon, freed the Seven Rivers, and drove the kine forth from the cave of Vala,
By whom this universe was made to tremble, who chased away the humbled brood of demons,
Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not.
Stirrer to action of the poor and lowly, of priest, of suppliant who sings his praises;
He under whose supreme control are horses, all chariots, and the villages, and cattle;
To whom two armies cry in close encounter, both enemies, the stronger and the weaker;
Without whose help our people never conquer; whom, battling, they invoke to give them succour;
He who hath smitten, ere they knew their danger, with his hurled weapon many grievous sinners;
He who discovered in the fortieth autumn Śambara as he dwelt among the mountains;
Who with seven guiding reins, the Bull, the Mighty, set free the Seven great Floods to flow at pleasure;
Even the Heaven and Earth bow down before him, before his very breath the mountains tremble.
Who aids with favour him who pours the Soma and him who brews it, sacrificer, singer.
Thou verily art fierce and true who sendest strength to the man who brews and pours libation.
WE call thee, Lord and Leader of the heavenly hosts, the wise among the wise, the famousest of all,
Bṛhaspati, God immortal! verily the Gods have gained from thee, the wise, a share in holy rites.
When thou hast chased away revilers and the gloom, thou mountest the refulgent car of sacrifice;
Thou leadest with good guidance and preservest men; distress o’ertakes not him who offers gifts to thee.
No sorrow, no distress from any side, no foes, no creatures double-tongued have overcome the man,—
Thou art our keeper, wise, preparer of our paths: we, for thy service, sing to thee with hymns of praise.
Him, too, who threatens us without offence of ours, the evilminded, arrogant, rapacious man,—
Thee as protector of our bodies we invoke, thee, saviour, as the comforter who loveth us.
Through thee, kind prosperer, O Brahmaṇaspati, may we obtain the wealth of Men which all desire:
With thee as our own rich and liberal ally may we, Bṛhaspati, gain highest power of life.
Strong, never yielding, hastening to the battle-cry, consumer of the foe, victorious in the strife,
Whoso with mind ungodly seeks to do us harm, who, deeming him a man of might mid lords, would slay,—
The mover mid the spoil, the winner of all wealth, to be invoked in fight and reverently adored,
Burn up the demons with thy fiercest flaming brand, those who have scorned thee in thy manifested might.
Bṛhaspati, that which the foe deserves not which shines among the folk effectual, splendid,
Give us not up to those who, foes in ambuscade, are greedy for the wealth of him who sits at ease,
For Tvaṣṭar, he who knows each sacred song, brought thee to life, preeminent o’er all the things that be.
The mountain, for thy glory, cleft itself apart when, Aṅgiras! thou openedst the stall of kine.
O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou controller of this our hymn and prosper thou our children.
THIS laud of the self-radiant wise Āditya shall be supreme o’er all that is in greatness.
Having extolled thee. Varuṇa, with thoughtful care may we have high fortune in thy service,
May we be in thy keeping, O thou Leader wide-ruling Varuṇa, Lord of many heroes.
He made them flow, the Āditya, the Sustainer: the rivers run by Varuṇa's commandment.
Loose me from sin as from a bond that binds me: may we swell, Varuṇa, thy spring of Order.
Far from me, Varuṇa, remove all danger accept me graciously, thou Holy Sovran.
Strike us not, Varuṇa, with those dread weapons which, Asura, at thy bidding wound the sinner.
O mighty Varuṇa, now and hereafter, even as of old, will we speak forth our worship.
Move far from me what sins I have committed: let me not suffer, King, for guilt of others.
O King, whoever, be he friend or kinsman, hath threatened me affrighted in my slumber-
May I not live O Varuṇa, to witness my wealthy, liberal dear friend's destitution.
FATHER of Maruts, let thy bliss approach us: exclude us not from looking on the sunlight.
With the most saving medicines which thou givest, Rudra, may I attain a hundred winters.
Chief of all born art thou in glory, Rudra, armed with the thunder, mightiest of the mighty.
Let us not anger thee with worship, Rudra, ill praise, Strong God! or mingled invocation.
May I with praise-songs win that Rudra's favour who is adored with gifts and invocations.
The Strong, begirt by Maruts, hath refreshed me, with most invigorating food, imploring.
Where is that gracious hand of thine, O Rudra, the hand that giveth health and bringeth comfort,
To him the strong, great, tawny, fair-complexioned, I utter forth a mighty hymn of praises.
With firm limbs, multiform, the strong, the tawny adorns himself with bright gold decorations:
Worthy, thou carriest thy bow and arrows, worthy, thy manyhued and honoured necklace.
Praise him the chariot-borne, the young, the famous, fierce, slaying like a dread beast of the forest.
I bend to thee as thou approachest, Rudra, even as a boy before the sire who greets him.
Of your pure medicines, O potent Maruts, those that are wholesomest and health-bestowing,
May Rudra's missile turn aside and spare us, the great wrath of the impetuous One avoid us.
O tawny Bull, thus showing forth thy nature, as neither to be wroth, O God, nor slay us.
EAGER for spoil my flow of speech I utter: may the Floods' Child accept my songs with favour.
To him let us address the song well-fashioned, forth from the heart. Shall he not understand it'
Some floods unite themselves and others join them: die sounding rivers fill one common storehouse.
The never-sullen waters, youthful Maidens, carefully decking, wait on him the youthful.
To him three Dames are offering food to feed him, Goddesses to the God whom none may injure.
Here was the horse's birth; his was the sunlight. Save thou our princes from the oppressor's onslaught.
He, in whose mansion is the teeming Milch-cow, swells the Gods’ nectar and cats noble viands.
He who in waters with his own pure Godhead shines widely, law-abiding, everlasting—
The Waters’ Son hath risen, and clothed in lightning ascended up unto the curled cloud's bosom;
Golden in form is he, like gold to look on, his colour is like gold, the Son of Waters.
This the fair name and this the lovely aspect of him the Waters’ Son increase in secret.
Him, nearest Friend of many, will we worship with sacrifice. and reverence and oblation.
The Bull hath laid his own life-germ Within them. He sucks them as an infant, and they kiss him.
While here he dwelleth in sublimest station, resplendent with the rays that never perish,
Agni, I gave good shelter to the people, and to the princes goodly preparation.
UPRISEN is Savitar, this God, to quicken, Priest who neglects not this most constant duty.
Having gone up on high, the God broad-handed spreads his arms widely forth that all may mark him.
Though borne by swift steeds he will yet unyoke them: e’en the fleet chariot hath he stayed from going.
What was spread out she weaves afresh, re-weaving: the skilful leaves his labour half-completed.
Through various dwellings, through entire existence, spreads, manifest, the household light of Agni.
He comes again, unfolded, fain for conquest: at home was he, the love of all things moving.
The wild beasts spread through desert places seeking their watery share which thou hast set in waters.
With utmost speed, in restless haste at sunset Varuṇa seeks his watery habitation.
Him whose high law not Varuṇa nor Indra, not Mitra, Aryaman, nor Rudra breaketh,
May they who strengthen bliss, and thought and wisdom, and the Dames’ Lord and Narāśaṁsa aid us.
So come to us our hearts' desire, the bounty bestowed by thee, from heaven and earth and waters,
O VĀYU, come to us with all the thousand chariots that are thine,
Drawn by thy team, O Vāyu, come; to thee is offered this, the pure.
Indra and Vāyu, drawn by teams, ye Heroes, come today and drink.
This Soma hath been shed for you, Law-strengtheners, Mitra-Varuṇa!
Both Kings who never injure aught seat them in their supremest home,
Fed with oblation, Sovran Kings, Ādityas, Lords of liberal gifts.
With kine, Nāsatyas, and with steeds, come, Aśvins, Rudras, to the house
Such, wealthy Gods! as none afar nor standing nigh to us may harm,
As such, O longed-far Aśvins, lead us on to wealth of varied sort,
Verily Indra, conquering all, driveth e’en mighty fear away,
Indra be gracious unto us: sin shall not reach us afterward,
From all the regions of the world let Indra send security,
O all ye Gods, come hitherward: hear this mine invocation, seat
Among the Śunahotras strong for you is this sweet gladdening draught.
Ye [Maruts](https://www.sacred-texts.com/hin/rigveda/errata.htm#13) led by Indra, Gods with Pūṣan for your bounteousest,
Best Mother, best of Rivers, best of Goddesses, Sarasvatī, We are, as ’twere, of no repute and dear Mother, give thou us renown.
In thee, Sarasvatī, divine, all generations have their stay.
Enriched with sacrifice, accept Sarasvatī, these prayers of ours,
Ye who bless sacrifice, go forth, for verily we choose you both,
This our effectual sacrifice, reaching the sky, shall Heaven and Earth
In both your laps, ye guileless Ones, the Holy Gods shall sit them down
THOU, Agni, who wilt have the strong, hast made me the Soma's priest, to worship in assembly.
East have we turned the rite; may the hymn aid it. With wood and worship shall they honour Agni.
The Prudent, he whose will is pure, brought welfare, allied by birth to Heaven and Earth in kinship.
Him, Blessed One, the Seven strong Floods augmented, him white at birth and red when waxen mighty.
Spreading with radiant limbs throughout the region, purging his power with wise purifications,
He sought heaven's Mighty Ones, the unconsuming, the unimpaired, not clothed and yet not naked.
His piles, assuming every form, are scattered where flow sweet waters, at the spring of fatness;
Carefully cherished, Son of Strength, thou shoncst assuming lasting and refulgent beauties.
From birth he knew even his Father's bosom, he set his voices and his streams in motion;
He nursed the Infant of the Sire and Maker: alone the Babe sucked many a teeming bosom.
The Mighty One increased in space unbounded; full many a glorious flood gave strength to Agni.
As keen supporter where great waters gather, light-shedder whom the brood rejoice to look on;
Him, varied in his form, the lovely Infant of floods and plants the blessed wood hath gendered.
Like brilliant lightnings, mighty luminaries accompany the light-diffusing Agni,
I sacrificing serve thee with oblations and crave with longing thy good-will and friendship.
May we, O Agni, thou who leadest wisely, thy followers and masters of all treasures,
Ensign of Gods hast thou become, O Agni, joy-giver, knower of all secret wisdom.
Within the house hath sate the King immortal of mortals, filling full their sacred synods.
Come unto us with thine auspicious friendship, come speeding, Mighty, with thy mighty succours.
To thee who art of old these songs, O Agni, have I declared, the ancient and the later.
Stablished in every birth is Jātavedas, kindled perpetual by the Viśvāmitras.
This sacrifice of ours do thou, O Mighty, O truly Wise, bear to the Gods rejoicing.
As holy food, Agni, to thine'invoker give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels.
FORTH from the bosom of the mountains, eager as two swift mares with loosened rein contending,
Impelled by Indra whom ye pray to urge you, ye move as ’twere on chariots to the ocean.
I have attained the most maternal River, we have approached Vipāś, the broad, the blessed.
We two who rise and swell with billowy waters move forward to the home which Gods have made us.
Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey.
Indra who wields the thunder dug our channels: he smote down Vṛtra, him who stayed our currents.
That hero deed of Indra must be lauded for ever that he rent Ahi in pieces.
Never forget this word of thine, O singer, which future generations shall reecho.
List quickly, Sisters, to the bard who cometh to you from far away with car and wagon.
Yea, we will listen to thy words, O singer. With wain and car from far away thou comest.
Soon as the Bharatas have fared across thee, the warrior band, urged on and sped by Indra,
The warrior host, the Bharatas, fared over the singer won the favour of the Rivers.
So let your wave bear up the pins, and ye, O Waters, spare the thongs;
To him adorable, mighty, meet for synods, this strengthening hymn, unceasing, have they offered.
To mighty Heaven and Earth I sing forth loudly: my wish goes out desirous and well knowing
O Heaven and Earth, may your great law he faithful: he ye our leaders for our high advantage.
Yea, holy Heaven and Earth, the ancient sages whose word was ever true had power to find you;
What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it?
The Sage who looketh on mankind hath viewed them bedewed, rejoicing in the seat of Order.
Partners though parted, with far-distant limits, on one firm place both stand for ever watchful,
All living things they part and keep asunder; though bearing up the mighty Gods they reel not.
Afar the Ancient from of old I ponder, our kinship with our mighty Sire and Father,—
This laud, O Heaven and Earth, to you I utter: let the kind-hearted hear, whose tongue is Agni,
The fair-tongued Savitar, the golden-handed, comes thrice from heaven as Lord in our assembly.
Deft worker, skiful-handed, helpful, holy, may Tvaṣṭar, God, give us these things to aid us,
Borne on their flashing car, the spear-armed Maruts, the nimble Youths of Heaven, the Sons of Order,
To Viṣṇu rich in marvels, songs And praises shall go as singers on the road of Bhaga,—
Indra, who rules through all his powers heroic, hath with his majesty filled earth and heaven.
My Sires are the Nāsatyas, kind tokinsmen: the Aśvins' kinship is a glorious title.
This is, ye Wise, your great and glorious title, that all ye Deities abide in Indra.
Aryaman, Aditi deserve our worship: the laws of Varuṇa remain unbroken.
May the Gods’ envoy, sent to many a quarter, proclaim us sinless for our perfect safety.
Hear us the mouatains which distil the rain-drops, and, resting firm, rejoice in freshening moisture.
Soft be our path for ever, well-provisioned: with pleasant meath, O Gods, the herbs besprinkle.
Enjoy the offering: beam thou strength upon us; combine thou for our good all kinds of glory.
MITRA, when speaking, stirreth men to labour: Mitra sustaineth both the earth and heaven.
Foremost be he who brings thee food, O Mitra, who strives to keep thy sacred Law, Āditya.
joying in sacred food and free from sickness, with knees bent lowly on the earth's broad surface,
Auspicious and adorable, this Mitra was born with fair dominion, King, Disposer.
The great Āditya, to be served with wor. ship, who stirreth men, is gracious to the singer.
The gainful grace of Mitra,. God, supporter of the race of man,
Mitra whose glory spreads afar, he who in might surpasses heaven,
All the Five Races have repaired to Mitra, ever strong to aid,
Mitra to Gods, to living men, to him who strews the holy grass,
YOUR well-known prompt activities aforetime needed no impulse from your faithful servant.
This man, most diligent, seeking after riches, incessantly invokes you for your favour.
O Indra-Varuṇa, ours be this treasure ours be wealth, Maruts, with full store of heroes.
Be pleased! with our oblations, thou loved of all Gods, Bṛhaspati:
At sacrifices, with your hymns worship the pure Bṛhaspati—
The Bull of men, whom none deceive, the wearer of each shape at will,
Divine, resplendent Pūṣan, this our newest hymn of eulogy,
Accept with favour this my song, be gracious to the earnest thought,
May he who sees all living things, see, them together at a glance,—
May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God:
With understanding, earnestly, of Savitar the God we crave
Men, singers worship Savitar the God with hymn and holy rites,
Soma who gives success goes forth, goes to the gathering place of Gods,
To us and to our cattle may Soma give salutary food,
May Soma, strengthening our power of life, and conquering our foes,
May Mitra-Varuṇa, sapient Pair, bedew our pasturage with oil,
Far-ruling, joyful when adored, ye reign through majesty of might,
Lauded by Jamadagni's song, sit in the place of holy Law:
As such, O Agni, bring with favour to the Gods thy Brother Varuṇa who loveth sacrifice,
Do thou, O Friend, turn hither him who is our Friend, swift as a wheel, like two car-steeds in rapid course, Wondrous! to us in rapid course.
Do thou who knowest Varuṇa, O Agni, put far away from us the God's displeasure.
Be thou, O Agni, nearest us with succour, our closest Friend while now this Morn is breaking.
Excellent is the glance, of brightest splendour, which the auspicious God bestows on mortals-
Three are those births, the true, the most exalted, eagerly longed-for, of the God, of Agni.
This envoy joyeth in all seats of worship, borne on his golden car, sweet-tongued Invoker:
Allied by worship, let him give man knowledge: by an extended cord they lead him onward.
Let Agni -for he knows the way- conduct us to all that he enjoys of God-sent riches,
In houses first he sprang into existence, at great heaven's base, and in this region's bosom;
Wondrously first he rose aloft, defiant, in the Bull's lair, the homeof holy Order,
Here did our human fathers take their places, fain to fulfil the sacred Law of worship.
Splendid were they when they had rent the mountain: others, around, shall tell forth this their exploit.
Eager, with thought intent upon the booty, the men with their celestial speech threw open,
The Milch-cow's earliest name they comprehended: they found the Mother's thrice-seven noblest titles.
The turbid darkness fled, the heaven was sp, endid! up rose the bright beam of celestial Morning.
Then, afterwards they looked around, awakened, when first they held that Heaven allotted treasure.
I will call hither brightly-beaming Agni, the Herald, all-supporting, best at worship.
The freest God of all who should be worshipped, the guest who is received in all men's houses,
I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Sūrya: I am the sage Kakṣīvān, holy singer.
I have bestowed the earth upon the Ārya, and rain upon the man who brings oblation.
In the wild joy of Soma I demolished Śambara's forts, ninety-and-nine, together;
Before all birds be ranked this Bird, O Maruts; supreme of falcons be this fleet-winged Falcon,
When the Bird brought it, hence in rapid motion sent on the wide path fleet as thought he hurried.
Bearing the stalk, the Falcon speeding onward, Bird bringing from afar the draught that gladdens,
The Falcon took and brought the Soma, bearing thousand libations with him, yea, ten thousand.
LET us recite the praise of Dadhikrāvan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion;
Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn.
His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim,
Bound by the neck and by the flanks and by the mouth, the vigorous Courser lends new swiftness to his speed.
The Haṁsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest,
Him who with might hath propped earth's ends, who sitteth in threefold seat, Bṛhaspati, with thunder,
Wild in their course, in well-marked wise rejoicing were they, Bṛhaspati, who pressed around us.
Bṛhaspati, from thy remotest distance have they sat down who love the law eternal.
Bṛhaspati, when first he had his being from mighty splendour in supremest heaven,
With the loud-shouting band who sang his praises, with thunder, he destroyed obstructive Vala.
Serve we with sacrifices, gifts, and homage even thus the Steer of all the Gods, the Father.
Surely that King by power and might heroic hath made him lord of all his foes' posses-ions,
In his own house he dwells in peace and comfort: to him for ever holy food flows richly.
He, unopposed, is master of the riches of his own subjects and of hostile people.
Indra, Bṛhaspati, rainers of treasure, rejoicing at this sacrifice drink the Soma.
Bṛhaspati and Indra, make us prosper may this be your benevolence to us-ward.
FORTH from the darkness in the region eastward this most abundant splendid light hatb mounted.
The richly-coloured Dawns have mounted eastward, like pillars planted at our sacrifices,
Dispelling gloom this day the wealthy Mornings urge liberal givers to present their treasures.
O Goddesses, is this your car, I ask you, ancient this day, or is it new, ye Mornings,
With horses harnessed by eternal Order, Goddesses, swiftly round the worlds ye travel,
Which among these is eldest, and where is she through whom they fixed the Ṛbhus' regulations?
Blest were these Dawns of old, shining with succour, true with the truth that springs from holy Order;
Hither from eastward all at once they travel, from one place spreading in the selfsame manner.
Thus they go forth with undiminished colours, these Mornings similar, in self-same fashion,
O Goddesses, O Heaven's refulgent Daughters, bestow upon us wealth with store of children.
Well-skilled in lore of sacrifice, ye Daughters of Heaven, refulgent Dawns, I thus address you.
FORTH from the ocean sprang the wave of sweetness: together with the stalk it turned to Amṛta,
Let us declare aloud the name of Ghṛta, and at this sacrifice hold it up with homage.
Four are his horns, three are the feet that bear him; his heads are two, his hands are seven in number.
That oil in triple shape the Gods discovered laid down within the Cow, concealed by Paṇis.
From inmost reservoir in countless channels flow down these rivers which the foe beholds not.
Like rivers our libations flow together, cleansing themselves in inmost heart and spirit.
As rushing down the rapids of a river, flow swifter than the wind the vigorous currents,
Like women at a gathering fair to look on and gently smiling, they incline to Agni.
As maidens dock themselves with gay adornment to join the bridal feast, I now behold them.
Send to our eulogy a herd of cattle bestow upon us excellent possessions.
The universe depends upon thy power and might within the sea, within the heart, within all life.
Agni is wakened by the people's fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow.
For worship of the Gods the Priest was wakened: at morning gracious Agni hath arisen.
When he hath stirred the line of his attendants, with the pure milk pure Agni is anointed.
The spirits of the pious turn together to Agni, as the eyes of all to Sūrya.
The noble One was born at days' beginning, laid red in colour mid the well-laid fuel.
Agni hath sat him down, a Priest most skilful, on a sweet-smelling place, his Mother's bosom.
This Singer excellent at sacrifices, Agni the Priest, they glorify with homage.
He, worshipful House-Friend, in his home is worshipped, our own auspicious guest, lauded by sages.
Thou quickly passest by all others, Agni, for him to whom thou hast appeared most lovely,
To thee, Most Youthful God! to thee, O Agni from near and far the people bring their tribute.
Ascend to-day thy splendid car, O Agni, in splendour, with the Holy Ones around it.
To him adorable, sage, strong and mighty we have sung forth our song of praise and homage.
URGING to toil and making proclamation, seeking Heaven's Daughter comes the Mighty Mother:
Swift in their motion, hasting to their duty, reaching the central point of life immortal,
Steer, Sea, Red Bird with strong wings, he hath entered the dwelling-place of the Primeval Father.
Four bear him up and give him rest and quiet, and ten invigorate the Babe for travel.
Wondrous, O people, is the mystic knowledge that while the waters stand the streams are flowing:
For him they lenghten prayers and acts of worship: the Mothers weave garments for him their offspring.
Be this our praise, O Varuṇa and Mitra may this be health and force to us, O Agni.
WITH all assistants, Agni, come hither to drink the Soma-juice;
Come to the sacrifice, O ye whose ways are right, whose laws are true,
O Singer, with the singers, O Gracious, with those who move at dawn,
To Indra and to Vāyu dear, this Soma, by the mortar pressed,
Vāyu, come hither to the feast, wellpleased unto our sacred gifts:
Ye, Indra, Vāyu, well deserve to drink the juices pressed by us.
For Indra and for Vāyu pressed are Soma juices blent with curd,
Associate with all the Gods, come, with the Aśvins and with Dawn,
Associate with Varuṇa, with Mitra, Soma, Viṣṇu, come,
Associate with Vasus, with Ādityas, Indra, Viyu, come, Agni as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.
May Bhaga and the Aśvins grant us health and wealth, and Goddess Adid and he whom none resist.
Let us solicit Vāyu for prosperity, and Soma who is Lord of all the world for weal;
May all the Gods, may Agni the beneficent, God of all men, this day be with us for our weal.
Prosper us, Mitra, Varuṇa. O wealthy Pathya, prosper us.
Like Sun and Moon may we pursue in full prosperity our path,
GUARDIANS of Order, ye whose Laws are ever true, in the sublimest heaven your chariot ye ascend.
This world's imperial Kings, O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye rule in holy synod, looking on the light.
Imperial Kings, strong, Heroes, Lords of earth and heaven, Mitra and Varuṇa, ye ever active Ones,
Your magic, Mitra-Varuṇa, resteth in the heaven. The Sun, the wondrous weapon, cometh forth as light.
The Maruts yoke their easy car for victory, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as a hero in the wars.
Refreshing is your voice, O Mitra-Varuṇa: Parjanya sendeth out a wondrous mighty voice.
Wise, with your Law and through the Asura's magic power ye guard the ordinances, Mitra-Varuṇa.
WE crave of Savitar the God this treasure much to be enjoyed.
Savitar's own supremacy, most glorious and beloved of all,
For Savitar who is Bhaga shall send riches to his worshipper.
Send us this day, God Savitar, prosperity with progeny.
Savitar, God, send far away all sorrows and calamities,
Sinless in sight of Aditi through the God Savitar's influence,
We with our hymns this day elect the general God, Lord of the good,
He who for ever vigilant precedes these Twain, the Day and Night,
He who gives glory unto all these living creatures with the song,
SING forth a hymn sublime and solemn, grateful to glorious. Varuṇa, imperial Ruler,
In the tree-tops the air he hath extended, put milk in kine and vigorous speed in horses,
Varuṇa lets the big cask, opening downward, flow through the heaven and earth and air's mid-region.
When Varuṇa is fain for milk he moistens the sky, the land, and earth to her foundation.
I will declare this mighty deed of magic, of glorious Varuṇa the Lord Immortal,
None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God's mighty deed of magic,
If we have sinned against the man who loves us, have ever wronged a brother, friend, or comrade,
If we, as gamesters cheat at play, have cheated, done wrong unwittingly or sinned of purpose,
THOU, first inventor of this prayer, O Agni, Worker of Marvels, hast become our Herald.
As Priest thou sattest at the seat of worship, furthering us, best Offerer, meet for honour.
In thee, still watching, they have followed riches, who goest with much wealth as with an army,
They who approached the God's abode with homage, eager for glory, won them perfect glory:
On earth the people magnify thee greatly, thee their celestial and terrestrial riches.
Dear priest among mankind, adorable Agni hath seated him, joy-giver, skilled in worship.
Longing for bliss, pure-minded, God-devoted, Agni, we seek thee, such, meet to be lauded.
Sage of mankind, all peoples' Lord and Master, the Bull of men, the sender down of blessings,
Agni, the mortal who hath toiled and worshipped, brought thee oblations with his kindled fuel,
Mightily let us worship thee the Mighty, with reverence, Agni! fuel and oblations,
Thou who hast covered heaven and earth with splendour and with thy glories, glorious and triumphant.
Vouchsafe us ever, as man needs, O Vasu, abundant wealth of kine for son and offspring.
May I obtain much wealth in many places by love of thee and through thy grace, King Agni;
YEA, this is good to taste and full of. sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour.
This sweet juice here had mightiest power to gladden: it boldened Indra when he siaughtered Vṛtra,
This stirreth up my voice when I have drunk it: this hath aroused from sleep my yearning spirit.
This, even this, is he who hath created the breadth of earth, the lofty height of heaven.
He found the wavy sea of brilliant colours in forefront of the Dawns who dwell in brightness.
Drink Soma boldly from the beaker, Indra, in war for treasures, Hero, Vṛtra-slayer!
Look out for us, O Indra, as our Leader, and guide us on to gain yet goodlier treasure.
Lead us to ample room, O thou who knowest, to happiness, security, and sunlight.
Set us on widest chariot-seat, O Indra, with two steeds best to draw, O Lord of Hundreds!
Be gracious, Indra, let my days be lengthened: sharpen my thought as ’twere a blade of iron
Indra the Rescuer, Indra the Helper, Hero who listens at each invocation,
May helpful Indra as our good Protector, Lord of all treasures, favour us with succour,
May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, may we dwell in his auspicious favour.
Like rivers rushing down a slope, O Indra, to thee haste songs and prayers and linked verses.
Who lauds him, satisfies him, pays him worship? E’en the rich noble still hath found him mighty.
Famed is the Hero as each strong man's tamer, ever advancing one and then another.
He loves no more the men he loved aforetime: he turns and moves away allied with others.
In every figure he hath been the mode: this is his only form for us to look on.
Here Tvaṣṭar, yoking to the car the Bay Steeds, hath extended sway.
Gods, we have reached a country void of pasture the land, though spacious, was too small to hold us.
Day after day far from their seat he drove them, alike, from place to place, those darksome creatures.
Out of thy bounty, Indra, hath Prastoka bestowed ten coffers and ten mettled horses.
Ten horses and ten treasure-chests, ten garments as an added gift,
Ten cars with extra steed to each, for the Atharvans hundred cows,
Thus Sṛñjaya's son honoured the Bharadvājas, recipients of all noble gifts and bounty.
Lord of the wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious hero
Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood.
Thou Bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuṇa and Child of Mitra,—
Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee;
Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers.
Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle's signal.
O PUSAN, bring us to the man who knows, who shall direct us straight,
May we go forth with Pūṣan who shall point the houses out to us,
Unharmed is Pūṣan's chariot wheel; the box ne’er falleth to the ground,
Pūṣan forgetteth not the man who serveth him with offered gift:
May Pūṣan follow near our kine; may Pūṣan keep our horses safe:
Follow the kine of him who pours libations out and worships thee;
Let none be lost, none injured, none sink in a pit and break a limb.
Pūṣan who listens to our prayers, the Strong whose wealth is never lost,
Secure in thy protecting care, O Pūṣan, never may we fail.
From out the distance, far and wide, may Pūṣan stretch his right hand forth,
To Vadhryasva when. be worshipped her with gifts she gave fierce Divodāsa, canceller of debts.
She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.
Thou castest down, Sarasvatī, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Bṛsaya skilled in magic arts.
May the divine Sarasvatī, rich in her wealth, protect us well,
Whoso, divine Sarasvatī, invokes thee where the prize is set,
Aid us, divine Sarasvad, thou who art strong in wealth and power
Yea, this divine Sarasvatī, terrible with her golden path,
Whose limitless unbroken flood, swift-moving with a rapid rush,
She hath spread us beyond all foes, beyond her Sisters, Holy One,
Yea, she most dear amid dear stream, Seven-sistered, graciously inclined,
Guard us from hate Sarasvatī, she who hath filled the realms of earth,
Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must be
Marked out by majesty among the Mighty Ones, in glory swifter than the other rapid Streams,
Guide us, Sarasvatī, to glorious treasure: refuse us not thy milk, nor spurn us from thee.
INDRA and Viṣṇu, at my task's completion I urge you on with food and sacred service.
Ye who inspire all hymns, Indra and Viṣṇu, ye vessels who contain the Soma juices,
Lords of joy-giving draughts, Indra and Viṣṇu, come, giving gifts of treasure, to the Soma.
May your foe-conquering horses bring you hither, Indra and Viṣṇu, sharers of the banquet.
This your deed, Indra-Viṣṇu, must be lauded: widely ye strode in the wild joy of Soma.
Strengthened with sacred offerings, IndraViṣṇu, first eaters, served with worship ana oblation,
Drink of this meath, O Indra, thou, and Viṣṇu; drink ye your fill of Soma, Wonder-Workers.
Ye Twain have conquered, ne’er have yc been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished.
THE warrior's look is like a thunderous rain-cloud's, when, armed with mail, he seeks the lap of battle.
With Bow let us win kine, with Bow the battle, with Bow be victors in our hot encounters.
Close to his car, as fain to speak, She presses, holding her well-loved Friend in her embraces.
These, meeting like a woman and her lover, bear, mother-like, their child upon their bosom.
With many a son, father of many daughters, He clangs and clashes as he goes to battle.
Upstanding in the Car the skilful Charioteer guides his strong Horses on whithersoe’er he will.
Horses whose hoofs rain dust are neighing loudly, yoked to the Chariots, showing forth their vigour,
Car-bearer is the name of his oblation, whercon are laid his Weapons and his Armour.
In sweet association lived the fathers who gave us life, profound and strong in trouble,
The Brahmans, and the Fathers meet for Soma-draughts, and, graciously inclined, unequalled Heaven and Earth.
Her tooth a deer, dressed in an eagle's feathers, bound with cow-hide, launched forth, She flieth onward.
Avoid us thou whose flight is straight, and let our bodies be as stone.
He lays his blows upon their backs, he deals his blows upon their thighs.
It compasses the arm with serpent windings, fending away the friction of the bowstring:
Now to the Shaft with venom smeared, tipped with deer-horn, with iron mouth,
Loosed from the Bowstring fly away, thou Arrow, sharpened by our prayer.
There where the flights of Arrows fall like boys whose locks are yet unshorn.
Thy vital parts I cover with thine Armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee.
Whoso would kill us, whether he be a strange foe or one of us,
THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands' swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni,
The Vasus set that Agni in the dwelling, fair to behold, for help from every quarter:
Shine thou before us, Agni, well-enkindled, with flame, Most Youthful God, that never fadeth.
Among all fires these fires have shone most brightly, splendid with light, begirt by noble heroes,
Victorious Agni, grant us wealth with wisdom, wealth with brave sons, famous and independent,
To whom, the Strong, at morn and eve comes, maid-like, the ladle dropping oil, with its oblation.
Burn up all malice with those flames, O Agni, wherewith of old thou burntest up Jarutha,
With him who lighteth up thy splendour, Agni, excellent, pure, refulgent, Purifier,
Agni, the patriarchal men, the mortals who have in many places spread thy lustre,—
Let these men, heroes in the fight with foemen, prevail against all godless arts of 4magic,—
Let us not sit in want of men, O Agni, without descendants, heroleu, about thee:
By sacrifice which the Steeds' Lord ever visits, there make our dwelling rich in seed and offspring,
Guard us, O Agni, from the hated demon, guard us from malice of the churlish sinner:
May this same fire of mine surpass all others, this fire where offspring, vigorous and firm-handed,
This is that Agni, saviour from the foeman, who guards the kindler of the flame from sorrow:
This is that Agni, served in many places, whom the rich lord who brings oblation kindles,
Agni, may we with riches in possession bring thee continual ofierings in abundance,
Agni, bear thou, Eternal, these most welcome oblations to the Deities' assembly:
Give us not up, Agni, to want of heroes, to wretched clothes, to need, to destitution.
Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on our chiefs and nobles.
Thou Agni, swift to hear, art fair of aspect: beam forth, O Son of Strength, in full effulgence.
Condemn us not to indigence, O Agni, beside these flaming fires which Gods have kindled;
O Agni, fair of face, the wealthy mortal who to the Immortal offers his oblation.
Knowing our chief felicity, O Agni, bring hither ample riches to our nobles,
Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on bur chiefs and nobles.
LET none, no, not thy worshippers, delay thee far away from us.
For here, like flies on honey, these who pray to thee sit by the juice that they have poured.
Longing for wealth I call on him, the Thunderer with the strong right hand,
These Soma juices, mixed with curd, have been expressed for Indra here.
May he whose ear is open hear us. He is asked for wealth: will he despise our prayer?
The hero never checked by men hath gained his strength through Indra, he
When thou dost drive the fighting men together be, thou Mighty One, the mighty's shield.
For Indra, Soma-drinker, armed with thunder, press the Soma juice.
Grudge not, ye Soma pourers; stir you, pay the rites, for wealth, to the great Conqueror.
No one hath overturned or stayed the car of him who freely gives.
Indra, that man when fighting shall obtain the spoil, whose strong defender thou wilt be.
His portion is exceeding great like a victorious soldier's spoil.
Make for the Holy Gods a hymn that is not mean, but well-arranged and fair of form.
Indra, what mortal will attack the man who hath his wealth in thee?
In battles with the foe urge on our mighty ones who give the treasures dear to thee,
Thine, Indra, is the lowest wealth, thou cherishest the mid-most wealth,
Thou art renowned as giving wealth to every one in all the battles that are fought.
If I, O Indra, were the Lord of riches ample as thine own,
Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in whatsoever place he were.
With Plenty for his true ally the active man will gain the spoil.
A moral wins no riches by unworthy praise: wealth comes not to the niggard churl.
Like kine unmilked we call aloud, Hero, to thee, and sing thy praise,
None other like to thee, of earth or of the heavens, hath been or ever will be born.
Bring, Indra, the Victorious Ones; bring, elder thou, the younger host.
Drive thou away our enemies, O Maghavan: make riches easy to be won.
O Indra, give us wisdom as a sire gives wisdom to his sons.
Grant that no mighty foes, unknown, malevolent, unhallowed, tread us to the ground.
FORTH from the middle of the flood the Waters-their chief the Sea-flow cleansing, never sleeping.
Waters which come from heaven, or those that wander dug from the earth, or flowing free by nature,
Those amid whom goes Varuṇa the Sovran, he who discriminates men's truth and falsehood-
They from whom Varuṇa the King, and Soma, and all the Deities drink strength and vigour,
WHOMSO ye rescue here and there, whomso ye guide, O Deities,
Through your kind favour, Gods, on some auspicious day, the worshipper subdues his foes.
Vasiṣṭha will not overlook the lowliest one among you all.
Your succour in the battle injures not the man to whom ye, Heroes, grant your gifts.
Come hitherward to drink the juice, O ye whose bounties give you joy.
Sit on our sacred grass, be graciously inclined to give the wealth for which we long,
Decking the beauty of their forms in secret the Swans with purple backs have flown down hither.
Maruts, the man whose wrath is hard to master, he who would slay us ere we think, O Vasus,
O Maruts, ye consuming Gods, enjoy this offering brought for you,
Sharers of household sacrifice, come, Maruts, stay not far away,
Here, Self-strong Maruts, yea, even here. ye Sages with your sunbright skins
Tryambaka we worship, sweet augmenter of prosperity.
COMMON to all mankind, auspicious Sūrya, he who beholdeth all, is mounting upward;
Sūrya's great ensign, restless as the billow, that urgeth men to action, is advancing:
Refulgent from the bosom of the Mornings, he in Whom singers take delight ascendeth.
Golden, far-seeing, from the heaven he riseth: far is his goal, he hasteth on resplendent.
Where the irrunortals have prepared his pathway he flieth through the region like a falcon.
Now Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman vouchsafe us freedom and room, for us and for our children.
THE Night retireth from the Dawn her Sister; the Dark one yieldeth to the Red her pathway.
Bearing rich treasure in your car, O Aśvins, come to the mortal who presents oblation.
May your strong horses, seeking bliss, bring hither your chariot at the earliest flush of morning.
The chariot, Princes, that conveys you, moving at daylight, triple-seated, fraught with riches,
Ye freed Cyavāna from old age and weakness: ye brought the courser fleet of food to Pedu.
This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins: accept this hymn of ours, ye Steers, With favour.
WISE, verily, are creatures through his greatness who stayed ever, spacious heaven and earth asunder;
With mine own heart I commune on the question how Varuṇa and I may be united.
Fain to know this is my sin I question others: I seek the wise, O Varuṇa, and ask them.
What, Varuṇa, hath been my chief transgression, that thou wouldst slay the friend who sings thy praises?
Free us from sins committed by our fathers, from those wherein we have ourselves offended.
Not our own will betrayed us, but seduction, thoughtlessness, Varuṇa wine, dice, or anger.
Slavelike may I do service to the Bounteous, serve, free from sin, the God inclined to anger.
O Lord, O Varuṇa, may this laudation come close to thee and lie within thy spirit.
LET me not yet, King Varuṇa, enter into the house of clay:
When, Thunderer! I move along tremulous like a wind-blown skin,
O Bright and Powerful God, through want of strength I erred and went astray
Thirst found thy worshipper though he stood in the midst of water-fijods:
O Varuṇa, whatever the offence may be which we as men commit against the heavenly host,
GLORIFY naught besides, O friends; so shall no sorrow trouble you.
Even him, eternal, like a bull who rushes down, men's Conqueror, bounteous like a cow;
Although these men in sundry ways invoke thee to obtain thine aid,
Those skilled in song, O Maghavan among these men o’ercome with might the foeman's songs.
O Caster of the Stone, I would not sell thee for a mighty price,
O Indra, thou art more to me than sire or niggard brother is.
